Method · source classes, claim relationships and anchor rules
Source-class key
Tier 1: primary record
Tier 2: research or academic source
Tier 3: trade press, aggregator or unclassified publisher
Tier 4: tool or data vendor
Tier 5: vendor publication or press office
This is a publisher class, not a trust score or a claim-relative relationship. Claim tiers are withheld unless the publisher relationship to the subject resolves.
Method and limits
  • Source-class tier is set from the publisher domain. It is not a truth or quality verdict.
  • Research Protocol intake may carry source_class_tier as routing metadata only. It cannot accept, reject or prioritise a claim.
  • A numeric claim tier appears only where a recorded owner or publisher relationship to the subject resolves. Otherwise the relationship remains unresolved.
  • Automatic topics may be plural. A portfolio anchor appears only when one candidate clears its threshold without a tie.
  • ArXiv, DOI and official links found in an article are typed as article-linked primaries. A link is not treated as proof that the document supports the headline.
Conflict of interest: an Anthropic model helped build the original method and tiers. An OpenAI model implemented the current source-class split, label provenance and anchor rules. OpenAI and Anthropic are subjects on the board. Neither model is an independent auditor of work from its own lab.
Tier registries: every class with its basis
Contest any cell: email NMAIResearch@proton.me or fork tier_map.json. Email a cell you dispute with the observable fact you think is wrong, or fork this file. Tiers change on evidence, not on disagreement with the conclusion.
Source classes
ClassTierObservable basis
primary record1record produced under a legal, statutory or official measurement process
research institute2research institute or academic source whose published method is the product
trade press3industry reporting funded by access, subscriptions or attention
aggregator3distribution layer rather than the originating evidence
tool or data vendor4sells tooling, data or research access connected to the topic
vendor publication5publishes about products, capabilities or markets in which the publisher participates
press office5institution publicising its own work
unclassified publisher3publisher class has not been resolved more specifically
Claim-relationship examples
EntityTierObservable basis
SEC / court / regulator filings1primary record produced under legal or statutory process; least incentive to shade a specific number
USGS / central-bank / agency data1mandated public measurement; the primary IS the check
US government / federal agencies (on AI)3Assess regulation, procurement and investment separately for the public body and claim concerned. Watch contains dated evidence and unresolved current-status checks; its archive preserves the earlier roster under dated-snapshot notices. Agency primary data retains its existing source classification.
Epoch AI2nonprofit research institute; credibility is the product. WATCH: funder prior (AI-safety mission may tilt framing toward 'AI is significant')
Peer-reviewed / arXiv (method claims)2method rigour (review, randomisation). WATCH: industry funding on the paper, and lag (rigour lands after the panic take)
Redwood Research / METR2independent AI evaluation orgs checking others' claims; incentive is being right, not selling a model
Gartner / Forrester / IDC / McKinsey3commercial analysts who sell reports AND consult the vendors they rate; round often-unfalsifiable forecasts
SemiAnalysis3independent analyst; data quality high but paywalls the conclusion that matters (access is the product)
Trade press (TechCrunch, VentureBeat, The Verge, Ars Technica)3industry journalism; access + engagement (conflict drives clicks). A take against the outlet's own audience usually carries less book
Reuters / Bloomberg / FT3wire / quality press; item-dependent, corroborate to the cited primary
Ahrefs / Semrush / SimilarWeb4SEO/analytics tool vendors; the data is often sound, the alarm framing helps sell the subscription
Anthropic (conflict disclosed)5sells frontier AI models; tier 5 on AI-value and its own-capability claims. Claim-relative: lower on unrelated facts
OpenAI (conflict disclosed)5sells frontier AI models; tier 5 on its own-capability and AI-value claims
Google / Google DeepMind5builds and sells the AI and the ad system the claim is often about
Meta5sells the platform and the models; tier 5 on its own-capability claims
Microsoft5sells the models and the cloud; tier 5 on its own-code-automation claims
Nvidia5sells the compute; tier 5 on 'is AI demand real'
Salesforce / Amazon / Snap (on own AI-efficiency)5adopters with an investor 'we are AI-efficient' narrative and a layoff justification; tier 5 on their own usage claims
NMAI Research (the author)2independent, no product tied to a market call, publishes reproducible CC-BY. Scored here rather than omitted: a motive map that exempts its own author is incomplete
The Anthropic model that helped build this (conflict disclosed)5a frontier-lab model helped assign these tiers, including the tiers on Anthropic and its rivals. Not exempt from its own map; corroborate its most consequential calls against a non-model source
The OpenAI model that helped maintain this (conflict disclosed)5a frontier-lab model implemented the current source-class split, label provenance, URL identity checks and anchor rules. OpenAI is a subject on the board, so this role is disclosed and is not treated as an independent audit of OpenAI-related output

Freshest data 2026-11-10. A small date after a cell means that cell is older: FRED indices run a trading day behind, and a market closed on a given day has no later price. Each percentage is the move since that series own previous observation, so a gap in the series is a longer window than a day. Context for the announced-vs-delivered lens, not a market call and not investment advice.
Coverage limit: this is a US-listed view of AI hardware, not the market for it
The quote source serves US and OTC ADR listings only, so the reachable China names are platform and cloud companies, not the domestic chipmakers. SMIC, Hua Hong, Cambricon, Samsung and SK Hynix cannot be shown here. OTC ADRs are thinly traded and can lag their home listing.
What that hides: the Shanghai STAR Market listings are where the domestic AI-chip complex is being repriced, and none of them are reachable at this data tier. Moore Threads closed its 5 December 2025 debut up about 425 per cent (offer 114.28 yuan, close 600.50), and MetaX opened up about 693 per cent on 17 December. Neither is a small move and neither can appear above. The absence is a limit of this data tier, not evidence that nothing is happening.
Method: source class comes from the executable public registry. A numeric claim tier is withheld unless the publisher relationship to the subject resolves. Figure labels state their method and complete-span coverage. Research-context links require one winning topic rule; tied candidates abstain. Feed selection is editorial and disclosed. This surfaces a structural weakness of a claim; it does not adjudicate truth.

Conflict of interest: the maker is an independent researcher. An Anthropic model helped build the original method and tiers. An OpenAI model later changed the matching, tier and provenance infrastructure. OpenAI is a subject on this board, so that work is a direct conflict and is disclosed rather than treated as an independent check. Anthropic and OpenAI remain subjects under the same published rules. Independent analysis, not investment advice.

Sourcing & method limits
Models that reached OpenRouter or the Hugging Face API in the window. Each row says whether the weights are published, which is an attribute of the release rather than a grade: an API-only model is shipped and serving traffic, it is simply not downloadable. Dates are when the model reached the source, not the vendor's own announcement date, and the Hugging Face dates are repo creation, which can sit either side of a public release. The two sides are not counted the same way, so the open and API-only totals are not comparable: OpenRouter is taken in full, while Hugging Face is a fixed list of labs capped at five repositories each. No benchmark scores, by choice. A model announced but never shipped cannot appear in any release list, including this one.

Sourcing & method limits
Audio and video engine releases, taken from the makers' own Hugging Face organisation lists: 11 organisations, each capped at 20 repositories. Whether a repository is audio or video is taken from the maker's own pipeline declaration where there is one, and from a word in the repository's name otherwise, which each row records as kind_from. A bare capability tag does not count, because a text model's tags can name video. The window is 180 days, not the 60 of the model release list, because these engines ship far less often, so the two totals are not comparable and are not added together. Every row here is an open-weights repository and the date is repo creation, which can sit either side of a public release. One launch published as several repositories reads as one row: a packaging copy (Diffusers, ONNX, GGUF, MLX, a quantised build) and a pretrained base twin fold into the earliest repository of that release and are counted in its folded field, while size and purpose variants such as medium and small-sfx keep their own rows. Control adapters, LoRAs and auxiliary parts are dropped, and so is a repository its own maker tags as watermarking or as an autoencoder, because a maker-owned repository is not automatically an engine release. A release whose own repository is older than the window is not shown even when a copy of it was published inside the window, so this is a count of releases and not of repository activity. The closed engines are missing by construction rather than by omission: Suno's music engine, Mureka, ElevenLabs and Sonauto published no keyless machine-readable release route when this was checked, which is listed beside the rows. A name-word filter also undercounts, because a release whose repository name carries no audio or video word is not shown, and a maker list cannot show a maker who is not on it. No benchmark scores, by choice.

Watch: evidence and upcoming decisions

Source checks: 2026-09-24. This calendar is manually maintained. Daily news refreshes do not update its evidence. A passed date does not resolve a question; all outcomes need a recorded source.

US government roles in AI: regulation, procurement and investment

An active subject for scrutiny: identify the public body, its powers and any financial or procurement relationship relevant to each AI claim. Dated evidence does not mean that the underlying issue has ended.

Assess statistical releases, forecasts, procurement decisions and investment announcements separately. A government interest can warrant scrutiny; it does not by itself establish that a statement is false or that every agency shares the same interest. No automatic source-tier change follows from this panel.

The records below establish what their dated sources report. They are not a complete current holdings register. Shares, preferred conversion rights, warrants, loans, guarantees, revenue sharing and proposals must remain distinct. The original roster is preserved in the dated archive below; its current status remains unverified.

Published date: 2026-09-25Brookings discussion of AI financing and policyUnresolved

Which assumptions and exposure gaps survive the research discussion?

Inspect
Conference draft, presentation and responses concerning investment scenarios, financing structures and the visibility of creditor exposures.
Evidence of improvement
Better measurements and explicit sensitivity checks narrow uncertainty.
Evidence of deterioration
Material exposure gaps persist or assumptions are contradicted by disclosed contracts and cash flows.
Limits
A research presentation is not a financial outcome or a forecast of collapse.
  • BPEA: 25 September, Panel on AI and Policy, including Financing the AI Buildout (conference organiser schedule)
Published date: 2026-09-30US Q2 GDP revision, industry data and August household incomeUnresolved

Is growth broadening, and can households sustain demand?

Inspect
Industry contributions, revisions, real disposable income, real consumption and saving. Adjust investment interpretation for imports.
Evidence of improvement
Broader domestic demand and improving real household income.
Evidence of deterioration
Growth concentrated in investment alongside weakening real income or consumption.
Limits
A revision describes an earlier quarter; it is not a September activity reading or a clean AI counterfactual.
  • BEA: September 30, October 29 and November 25 rows (primary calendar)
Published date: 2026-09-30Micron fiscal Q4 resultsUnresolved

Do reported orders and any customer prepayments lead to delivered supply and collected cash?

Inspect
Cash flow, any disclosed customer deposits and their repayment or financing terms, delivered memory and revised capacity plans.
Evidence of improvement
Disclosed cash receipts and delivery consistent with contractual milestones.
Evidence of deterioration
Deposit reversals, delivery slippage or financing needs growing faster than operating receipts.
Limits
An earnings call does not independently confirm customer acceptance; management forecasts remain forecasts.
  • MICRON: Opening paragraph, fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call (issuer calendar)

Are hiring conditions improving beyond a few sectors?

Inspect
Payroll revisions, unemployment, participation, hours and industry detail.
Evidence of improvement
Hiring and hours improve across industries without falling participation concealing weakness.
Evidence of deterioration
Downward revisions and weaker hiring or hours across several sectors.
Limits
US aggregate employment does not measure EU AI operations vacancies.

How do observed physical supply conditions compare with the latest price forecast?

Changes in production, inventories, export-route assumptions, refining and household fuel costs.
Evidence of improvement
Observed supply, inventories and household costs support a less constrained outlook.
Evidence of deterioration
Supply constraints or inventory declines undermine the forecast.

Editorial review: 2026-10-02Financing and refinancingUnresolved

Does cash generation cover operations and debt service without increasingly restrictive finance?

weekly and on new debt filings

Inspect
For CoreWeave, Oracle and selected infrastructure counterparties: debt actually drawn, fixed/floating mix, benchmark plus credit margin, cash interest, maturities, covenants, collateral, hedges, capitalised interest, equity dilution and customer prepayments.
Evidence of improvement
Operating receipts and contract renewals support repayments; like-for-like financing terms improve.
Evidence of deterioration
Cash interest rises faster than operating receipts; waivers, failed refinancing, contract loss or supplier payment delays appear.
Limits
The September convertible-note announcement verifies pricing, not completion. A low convertible coupon is not the total economic financing cost. Backlog is not cash.

Renewals at sustainable pricing, net customer savings after review and integration, and improving operating cash generation.

Registers: historical snapshot. Recorded 2026-08-02 . Not refreshed by the daily news pipeline; current status is unverified.

Deflation register (16)
Claims where the checkable figure came back different, with the correction and where it came from. This register grades the number, not the person. A figure taken from video or press is described by genre and register tier rather than named, so the claim line says where it circulates and is not an attribution; the checkable weight sits on the corrected line, which is what a reader should test. The dot is the tier carried by the public register row. Being wrong once is not a verdict on a source.
Bot web-traffic energy use
circulating via public/press [4]
Correction: ~15–20× lower (~15–20×)
3 methodological errors (see bot-energy v1.1, Zenodo 20707001)
"267%" data-centre power figure
circulating via press/aggregator [4]
Correction: excluded entirely
measures wholesale price at specific grid nodes, not a household bill
Spruce Pine HPQ "all chips depend on it" apocalypse
circulating via popular-chokepoint narrative [4]
Correction: not a live crisis
Helene hit it directly; production restarted ~10 days; absent from 12-mo sell-side notes
Neon supply shock (post-2022)
circulating via legacy-shock narrative [3]
Correction: no acute 2026 shortage
absorbed: China dominant, recycling >90%, fabs hold 1–12mo buffers; real risk is relocated concentration
Tesla Optimus "1M units/yr"
circulating via vendor [5]
Correction: ambition, not settled proof (claim ≠ deliverable)
no commercial-availability page; Musk admits "still R&D"
OpenAI "lost $38.5B in 2025"
circulating via YouTube capital-cycle video [4], off Zitron/FT [2]
Correction: operating loss $20.9B on $13.07B rev; cash burn ~$8B per one FT source (~1.8× (op) / ~4.8× (cash))
headline net loss carries a $41.55B NON-CASH charge from the nonprofit→for-profit conversion (revaluing convertibles + warrants). Cited as proof competition compressed returns: category error. The S&M line ($5.73B, +418%, 44% of rev) DOES survive
SPR "~20% operational floor → ~62 usable days"
circulating via MY OWN TRACKER [self]
Correction: no published hard floor: drawdown RATE degrades as caverns empty
"days to empty at max rate" is the wrong metric. The rival "160M bbl minimum" (TLDR video) attaches to the cancelled Richton MS site (160M capacity), not a reserve minimum. Compounded by GAO-26-106918: >25% of SPR oil cannot currently be surfaced
Pangram "1-in-10,000 false-positive rate"
circulating via vendor [5]
Correction: direction independently supported, the exact figure is not
UChicago Booth WP (Jabarian & Imas, BFI 2025-116) confirms ~zero FPR on long/medium text and a unique ability to hold a 0.5% policy cap, but does not reproduce 0.01%; degrades on short/unusual text; humanizers exist
"May PCE 4.1% = inflation surging / broad-based"
circulating via press/political panic [4]
Correction: Dallas trimmed-mean PCE FELL to 2.4% (from 2.6% a yr earlier)
the 4.1% headline is idiosyncratic energy + tariff + AI-goods spikes, NOT broad-based: the Fed's own trimmed-mean (drops the largest outliers each month) declined y/y even as headline hit a 3-yr high; the core-goods leg is AI-demand driven and tariff-EXEMPT. Fed MPR Jul-2026 [1]
Memory prices "+355% by the end of this year"
circulating via YouTube explainer [4], no source given
Correction: Gartner: +125% across 2026; DRAM +100-116% Q1-26; TrendForce +13-18% QoQ Q3-26, cooling from ~60% QoQ in Q2; Counterpoint 80-90% QoQ Q4-25→Q1-26 (~2.8× vs Gartner)
No source exists for 355%. Probable mechanism: a supply-partner note advising customers to "plan for 10-20% per month" compounded across a year lands near a triple-digit figure ⇒ a planning ceiling read as a forecast. Note the direction of the real data is decelerating (Q2 ~60% QoQ → Q3 13-18%) while the claim implies acceleration. Added 2026-07-17 from the transcript sweep (IBM video)
PJM 2028/29 capacity "spiking to the cap = fresh grid crisis"
circulating via grid-doom framing [4]
Correction: the $325/MW-day clear is −2.5% BELOW the prior cap = flat-high, NOT a spike; but the collar MASKED ~$13.3B (~1.8× (masked))
two-sided: the level is not a new spike (capped, down y/y), yet the collar hid a real ~$13.3B ($29.7B uncapped vs $16.4B actual) DC-driven cost: carry BOTH denominators (DC ~40% this auction / 45% = $21.3B of $47.2B over three). Monitoring Analytics. Added Session 5 from the §3.7② fold
LLM token index "fell ~50%"
circulating via YouTube AI-finance video [4]
Correction: −20% from its May peak (Silicon Data SDLLMTK, now ~1.62; ~doubled since Dec inception) (~2.5× (overstated))
direction right (willingness-to-pay per Mtoken falling as users substitute to cheaper models, per Citadel), magnitude ~2.5× overstated. Bankable real signal: Allianz flags a 46% AI investment-vs-sales growth gap vs 32% in the 2001 telecom bubble. Added 2026-07-18 (transcript sweep)
S&P top-10 concentration "~10% in 2000 vs 40% today"
circulating via YouTube market-valuation video [4]
Correction: ~23% in 2000 (Visual Capitalist; 20-25% across sources) vs ~36% today, off a ~41% peak in 2025 (~2.5× (the change, overstated))
Both ends wrong in the direction that inflates the change: the claim implies a 4× rise, the data show 23→36, roughly 1.6×. The honest version of the point survives and is stronger for being smaller. ⭐ The caveat the same video omits, which cuts the other way: in 2000 tech was ~33% of S&P market cap on only ~15% of its earnings; today's top-10 weight sits on real profits, so weight alone is not equivalent excess. Added 2026-07-29 (transcript sweep)
Margin debt "record $1.42T" as evidence of a top
circulating via YouTube market-valuation video [4], off FINRA [1]
Correction: level TRUE ($1.416T, May-2026, +8.5% m/m, +53.7% y/y), the INFERENCE fails on the denominator
⭐ Same numerator, opposite story depending on the base. Against market cap margin debt is ~2.2%, BELOW the 2000 peak (~2.3%) and well below 2007 (~3.0%). Against GDP (~4%) it IS a record, just past Oct-2021's 3.97%. The video quotes only the nominal record, which is the one base that guarantees a record in any year prices rise. Also stale by two months when quoted. What genuinely survives: leverage grew at ~2× the pace of the S&P over the same May-to-May window, and only 1999-2000, mid-2007 and spring 2021 saw comparable growth RATES. Added 2026-07-29
Banks tightening lending standards "~40% in 2023 → 8% today"
circulating via YouTube macro-strategy video [4], which books sales calls at the end
Correction: NOT CHECKABLE AS FRAMED, and the latest actual reading points the other way
The July-2026 SLOOS (Q2) is not published (the Fed releases it in early August), so no "today" figure exists. The most recent, April 2026, reports net TIGHTENING on C&I citing a less favourable outlook and reduced risk tolerance, plus tighter standards across all NDFI categories over the year. The video's entire "no recession, therefore buy the dip" thesis rests on this single series. ⚠️ SLOOS is reported as a net percentage (tightened minus eased), so a raw "8% of banks" reading would be a category error on top. Do not bank the 8%; re-check the series (FRED DRTSCILM) when the July release lands. Added 2026-07-29
"Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time ever on Friday"
circulating via YouTube market-valuation video [4]
Correction: first close above 50,000 was Fri 6 Feb 2026 (50,115.67); it first closed above 53,000 on 6 Jul
⭐ Logged as a VINTAGE catch, not an arithmetic one, because it dates the source. A video presenting a nearly six-month-old milestone as this week's news is either stale or splicing archival clips as current. Its Korea line ("bounced back above 7,000, Citi calls it a technical correction") was already dead when checked (6,023.66). ⇒ date-the-data applies to the SOURCE, not only to its figures: the same video's Buffett-indicator and margin-debt numbers checked out, so vintage failure is item-by-item, and each claim needs its own date. Added 2026-07-29
AI Watch: resolution calendar
Dated moments when an open, AI-relevant question resolves, each paired with the specific observable that settles it. These are not predictions. Each row states what to watch and the tell that decides it.
Resolution calendar
2 Aug 2026EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations take effect.
Settles on: First enforcement posture and guidance on AI-content transparency and disclosure duties.
late-Sep 2026Is household credit stress turning, or still easing?
Settles on: The Q2 2026 reading of credit-card delinquency at US commercial banks, published around late September because the series runs a quarter behind. Through Q1 2026 it fell every quarter to 2.92 percent, and at small banks outside the top 100 to 6.43 percent, narrowing the gap between them. A rise in either, or a widening gap, would be the turn.
1 Oct 2026Are the Colorado River's 2007 operating rules replaced before they expire?
Settles on: New interim operating guidelines agreed, or a deadlock. A deadlock raises litigation and water-siting risk for Western US data centres.
Related research: AI Data-Centre Water Tracker (DOI)
late-Oct 2026Did the memory squeeze defer enterprise software spending, or end it?
Settles on: IBM's Q3 results, reported through late October. Two numbers decide it: software growth against IBM's own 6 to 8 percent guide, and whether annual recurring revenue keeps growing from the 8 percent it added in Q2. Software printing below 6 percent, or recurring revenue decelerating, would mean the spending was lost rather than delayed.
late-Oct 2026Is the AI data-centre capital-expenditure boom still accelerating?
Settles on: Hyperscaler Q3 earnings, reported through late October: whether 2026 capital expenditure guidance is raised, held or cut, and what is said about high-bandwidth memory allocation for 2027. A held or cut guide would be the first crack. The Q2 round did not produce one, which is why this row was extended rather than closed.
Related research: Contingent vs Robust AI Power Demand (DOI)
10 Nov 2026Do US controls on lithography exports to China tighten in November?
Settles on: The Affiliates Rule suspension, a carve-out of the current trade truce, expires on 10 November. Three observables: whether it is renewed or allowed to lapse, whether the MATCH Act advances (it would bar all ASML deep-ultraviolet sales to China and start a 150-day clock on Dutch alignment), and what ASML's own guidance says about China revenue.
Related research: The AI Capital-Infrastructure Barbell (DOI)
27 Nov 2026Do China's rare-earth and neon export controls renew, widen or lapse?
Settles on: The renewal decision, with neon controls the specific trigger to watch.
Dec 2026Does data-centre load keep pinning the PJM capacity price at its cap?
Settles on: The 2030/31 base residual auction, the last one under the price collar. Three readings: how much new supply clears against the shortfall, whether the $325 per MW-day cap holds, and the data-centre share of capacity cost. For scale, the 2028/29 auction cleared about 525 MW against a 6,831 MW shortfall, with data centres carrying 40% of capacity cost in that auction.
Related research: Contingent vs Robust AI Power Demand (DOI)
2 Dec 2026EU AI Act Art. 50(2): does the marking grandfathering bite when it lapses?
Settles on: Whether generative AI systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 carry machine-readable marking and a detection route by the date the transitional period ends.
2 Dec 2027EU AI Act high-risk (Annex III) obligations take effect.
Settles on: The high-risk compliance regime comes into force.
Historical gauge readings
Strait of Hormuz risk (as of 2026-07-31)
Brent peaked at $105.32 on 23 July, held $100.31 on 24 July, then fell to $91.82 by 27 July, the most recent daily observation. The move up ran from a low of $68.53 on 2 July, so the round trip is roughly $37 up and $13 back inside four weeks. Source throughout: FRED series DCOILBRENTEU, Europe Brent spot, which is the same series the board's market strip reads.
Watch: The $100 level flagged here on 13 July was crossed on 23 July and did not hold. The tell moves on again: whether the July low near $68 or the July high near $105 is the better guide to Q4, and whether any renewed disruption puts it back through $100 rather than whether it gets there once.
This still runs against the forecast anchor, but by less than it did. The EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook base case of 7 July had Brent easing to about $70 by Q4 2026 as the tanker backlog cleared, and Rapidan raised its Q4 estimate to near $100 from $85. At $91.82 neither is settled. Goldman's above-$120 case required Hormuz disruption to persist, which on this price path it has not. The base case is recorded as contested, not withdrawn.

Tracking announced vs delivered
Pre-release commitments and unserved milestones. announced_date is when the commitment was made. last_verified is when the status was last checked against a primary or named source, and the two are different objects: an old announcement carried forward unchecked is not a live target. Disclosed conflict: the US government's three hats on AI
A government source commenting on AI holds three positions at once: it regulates the technology, buys it, and holds equity in the stack it comments on. A government AI claim therefore moves three books: policy, procurement and portfolio. Agency primary data (Federal Reserve, BLS, USGS) stays tier 1; this flag applies to government commentary and claims on AI.
Regulator. Gates model releases and sets AI policy (2026 safety-review holds on GPT-5.6 and Fable 5 / Mythos 5).
Customer. Procures AI and awards or withholds federal contracts (Anthropic reportedly frozen out of the stake talks and blocked from federal contracts, mid-2026).
Owner. Holds equity across the AI-buildout stack, and was offered a 5% stake in a model lab (OpenAI).
CFR tracker: roughly $20.9B across 17 equity or quasi-equity deals since Jan 2025 (a broader count reaches 28 firms once letters of intent are included). By dollars: semiconductors ~52%, critical minerals ~43%. Held equity below; revenue-share and proposed positions are kept separate so they are not miscounted.

Coding-harness landscape

A source-separated guide to public harness usage signals, catalogues and controlled benchmark methods. It does not combine unlike measures or select one best harness.
Sources are grouped by the question they can answer. No composite rank is calculated.
Usage, popularity, documented capability and controlled task performance describe different populations and denominators. A missing measure remains unassessed and no source is treated as proof of general quality.
Sources checked 2026-08-31 · 4 public source types
OpenLabor Harness Ranking ↗OpenRouter usage
Attributed OpenRouter tokens, requests and model share over selectable time windows.
Limit: This observes one routing channel. It does not establish active users, total adoption, privacy, safety or harness quality.
HarnessMatch ↗Source-separated comparison
Documented capabilities, operating models, evidence coverage and eight separate public usage views.
Limit: Its usage channels retain their native denominators. Popularity, capability and benchmark evidence are not added into one score.
Best of Agent Harnesses ↗Discovery catalogue
A curated project catalogue with categories, editorial attributes, activity signals and machine-readable data.
Limit: Its ordering uses editorial relevance and GitHub signals. It is useful for discovery, not a controlled adoption or performance benchmark.
HarnessRank ↗Method published, results pending
A same-benchmark, same-model and same-effort repeated-run comparison method.
Limit: No full benchmark rows were published at the checked date. The method is visible, but there is no result table to reproduce or rank.
Benchmark method references
Qihoo360 Harness-Bench ↗Method reference
Reference for deterministic outcomes, process measures, robustness, security and efficiency. Reuse requires a fresh licence check.
Harbor ↗Implementation substrate
A benchmark orchestration substrate, not a ranking authority. Telemetry, network behaviour and isolation require separate verification.
PLAG IN prototype compatibility snapshot
The earlier five-client compatibility order is retained only as a dated project note. It is not part of the independent harness landscape and does not rank harness quality.
No installed client completed a verified end-to-end integration in that snapshot. Later benchmark work requires its own evidence and approval.
